Use it to verify your loading states look right, check that the right content appears immediately, and iterate on where to place `` boundaries. 91 92 Enable the toggle in your Next.js config: 93 94 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5-7} 95 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 96 97 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 98 cacheComponents: true, 99 experimental: { 100 instantNavigationDevToolsToggle: true, 101 }, 102 } 103 104 export default nextConfig 105 ``` 106 107 Open the Next.js DevTools and select **Instant Navs**. "Checking availability..." shows where inventory will stream in. 115 116 > **Good to know:** Page loads and client navigations can produce different shells. Client-side hooks like `useSearchParams` suspend on page loads (search params are not known at build time) but resolve synchronously on client navigations (the router already has the params). 117 118
119 Why page loads and client navigations produce different shells 120 121 On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root, including all layouts. Anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `` boundary in the entire document tree. 122 123 On a client navigation (clicking `next/link`), Next.js only re-renders below the layout that the source and destination routes share. Components above that shared layout are not re-rendered. This means that a `` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but for a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, the shared layout is `/store` and Next.js renders the part of the document below that point. The root `` sits above it and does not trigger for this navigation. 124 125 This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during server rendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL and the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can appear in the instant shell on a client navigation but behind a fallback on a page load. 126 127
128 129 ## Prevent regressions with e2e tests 130 131 Validation catches structural problems during development and at build time. After the callback finishes, dynamic content streams in and you can assert on the full page. 151 152 There is no need to write an `instant()` test for every navigation. Build-time validation already provides the structural guarantee. Use `instant()` for the user flows that matter most. 153 154 ## Fixing a navigation that blocks 155 156 Now consider a different route, `/shop/[slug]`. After the callback finishes, dynamic content streams in and you can assert on the full page. 151 152 There is no need to write an `instant()` test for every navigation. Build-time validation already provides the structural guarantee. Use `instant()` for the user flows that matter most. 153 154 ## Fixing a navigation that blocks 155 156 Now consider a different route, `/shop/[slug]`. For the sake of this example it has the same data requirements as `/store/[slug]`, but is implemented without local `` boundaries or caching: 157 158 ```tsx filename="app/shop/[slug]/page.tsx" 159 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 160 161 export default async function ProductPage(props: PageProps<'/shop/[slug]'>) { 162 const { slug } = await props.params 163 const product = await db.products.findBySlug(slug) 164 const item = await db.inventory.findBySlug(slug) 165 return ( 166
167

{product.name}

168

${product.price}

169

{item.count} in stock

170
171 ) 172 } 173 ``` 174 175 The root layout wraps `{children}` in a `` boundary: 176 177 ```tsx filename="app/layout.tsx" highlight={9} 178 export default function RootLayout({ 179 children, 180 }: { 181 children: React.ReactNode 182 }) { 183 return ( 184 185 186 Loading...

}>{children} 187 188 189 ) 190 } 191 ``` 192 193 On an initial page load, the root `` catches the async work and streams the page in behind the `fallback`. 194 195 Everything appears to work. But on a client navigation from `/shop/shoes` to `/shop/hats`, the shared layout is `/shop` and only the content below it re-renders. The root `` boundary is above that layout and is not triggered for this navigation. The page fetches uncached data with no local boundary, blocking the navigation until the server finishes rendering. 196 197 You can see this with the DevTools. Try a **page load**: the root `` catches everything and "Loading..." appears. Now try a **client navigation** between two `/shop/` pages: no prefetched UI shows up because there is no `` boundary below the shared layout. Navigations from other routes to `/shop/` appear blocked too. 198 199 ### Step 1: Add instant validation 200 201 Add an `unstable_instant` export to the page to surface the problem: 202 203 ```tsx filename="app/shop/[slug]/page.tsx" highlight={3-6} 204 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 205 206 export const unstable_instant = { 207 prefetch: 'static', 208 samples: [{ params: { slug: 'example' } }], 209 } 210 211 export default async function ProductPage(props: PageProps<'/shop/[slug]'>) { 212 const { slug } = await props.params 213 const product = await db.products.findBySlug(slug) 214 const item = await db.inventory.findBySlug(slug) 215 return ( 216
217

{product.name}

218

${product.price}

219

{item.count} in stock

220
221 ) 222 } 223 ``` 224 225 Next.js now simulates navigations at every shared layout boundary in the route. In this case, both components await `params` and access uncached data. These need to be wrapped by a `` boundary. The first thing validation catches is the `await params` at the top level. 226 227 ### Step 2: Fix the validation error 228 229 There is no `generateStaticParams` here, `slug` is only known at request time. Because awaiting `params` suspends, the page component can't do it at the top level. Instead, move the `await params` into separate components, pass `params` to each, and wrap them with ``. 230 231 For each component, decide: 232 233 **Product details** (name, price) rarely change. Cache the data function with `use cache`: 234 235 ```tsx filename="app/shop/[slug]/page.tsx" 236 async function ProductInfo({ params }: { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> }) { 237 const { slug } = await params 238 const product = await getProduct(slug) 239 return ( 240 <> 241

{product.name}

242

${product.price}

243 244 ) 245 } 246 247 async function getProduct(slug: string) { 248 'use cache' 249 return db.products.findBySlug(slug) 250 } 251 ``` 252 253 > **Good to know:** In serverless deployments, in-memory caching with `"use cache"` will not persist across instances. Consider using [`"use cache: remote"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-remote) for persistent caching. 254 255 **Inventory** must be fresh each request. Leave it uncached: 256 257 ```tsx filename="app/shop/[slug]/page.tsx" 258 async function Inventory({ params }: { params: Promise<{ slug: string }> }) { 259 const { slug } = await params 260 const item = await db.inventory.findBySlug(slug) 261 return

{item.count} in stock

262 } 263 ``` 264 265 The page passes `params` to each component and wraps them with ``: 266 267 ```tsx filename="app/shop/[slug]/page.tsx" highlight={4-7,12-17} 268 import { Suspense } from 'react' 269 import { db } from '@/lib/db' 270 271 export const unstable_instant = { 272 prefetch: 'static', 273 samples: [{ params: { slug: 'example' } }], 274 } 275 276 export default function ProductPage(props: PageProps<'/shop/[slug]'>) { 277 return ( 278

293 How validation simulates different navigations 294 295 When you add `unstable_instant` to a route, Next.js checks both the initial page load and client navigations at different points in the route hierarchy. 296 297 For a route like `/shop/[slug]`, validation checks: 298 299 - **Page load**: the full tree renders from the root. The root layout `` catches everything. 300 - **Client navigation** (e.g. from `/shop/shoes` to `/shop/hats`): the `/shop` layout is already mounted and only the page below it re-renders. A `` boundary in the root layout does not cover this navigation. 301 302 Each case is validated independently. A `` boundary that covers one navigation path might not cover another. This is why a page can pass the page load check but fail for client navigations, and why catching these issues by hand is difficult as the number of routes grows. 303 304
305 306 ## Opting out with `instant = false` 307 308 Not every layout or page can be instant. A dashboard layout that reads cookies and fetches user-specific data might be too dynamic for the first visit. You can set `instant = false` on any layout or page to exempt it from validation: 309 310 ```tsx filename="app/dashboard/layout.tsx" 311 export const unstable_instant = false 312 ``` 313 314 This tells validation: navigating to `/dashboard` from outside does not need to be instant, but sibling navigations within it still do. Navigating from `/dashboard/a` to `/dashboard/b` can still be checked by adding `instant` to the page segments under `/dashboard`. 315 316 ## Next steps 317 318 - [`instant` API reference](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant) for all configuration options, including runtime prefetching and incremental adoption with `instant = false` 319 - [Caching](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) for background on `use cache`, Suspense, and Partial Prerendering 320 - [Revalidating](/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating) for how to expire cached data with `cacheLife` and `updateTag` 321
